name: Long Coordination Gauntlet — 14-Move Single-Bell Conti Flow
description: A long, playful, single-bell kettlebell flow from a Madeleine Conti reel — fourteen moves chained one side, then repeated on the other. It mixes ballistic swings, cleans, and overhead work with lateral and curtsy lunges, and drops to a half-kneeling sub-sequence mid-flow before standing back up. It's intentionally long and a little confusing — the first goal is grooving the sequence, not loading it. Go LIGHT and keep it smooth; mind the right shoulder on the overhead beats (windmills, press, snatch, catch).
flowNotes: **This is a continuous 14-move FLOW, not separate stations — and it's a long one.** Move through the whole chain on ONE side, then repeat on the other. Because it's long and mixes a lot of skills (swings, cleans, overhead, lunges, and a half-kneeling drop-and-stand in the middle), treat it as **light Tuesday practice**: single LIGHT bell, 1–2 easy rounds per side, and the win is remembering the sequence, not the load or the round count. The tricky part is the half-kneeling sub-sequence (beats 9–12) where you lower to the floor and stand back up — walk that slowly. Overhead-heavy in spots (windmills, press, snatch, the catch), so pack the shoulder DOWN on every overhead beat and back off if the right shoulder flares.

flowSequence.notes: **Reverse Simple / Switch Swing:** single-arm swing that switches hands at the top float — release as the bell goes weightless, catch it cleanly with the other hand, then swing down and back. Hips drive it; the hand-switch is the skill. (Conti's 'reverse simple' — it's a switch / alternating swing.)
**Figure-8 Tactical Clean:** weave the bell through the legs in a figure-8, then exit that pass into a smooth tactical clean up to the rack — thread it, no forearm bang.

**Kickstand Thruster:** stagger the stance (one foot slightly back — the kickstand) with the bell racked; squat, then drive up and press overhead in one motion. The kickstand biases one leg and fights rotation.
**Windmill:** bell locked out overhead, eyes on it, push the hip out and hinge to the side, hand sliding down the front leg. Straight overhead arm, long spine — mobility + overhead stability.
**Lateral Lunge:** step wide to the side and sit into that hip, other leg straight, chest tall; drive back to center. Frontal-plane leg work (adductors, glute med).

**Tactical Clean → Curtsy Lunge:** clean the bell to the rack (controlled tactical clean), then step the working-side leg diagonally behind into a curtsy lunge while racked. Outer-glute biased; stay tall against the offset load.
**Overhead Press:** from the rack, one strict press to lockout — shoulder packed DOWN, ribs down, don't lean back to cheat it.

**Inside Rack → Outside Snatch + Forward Lunge:** from the rack, snatch the bell up on the outside path to overhead while stepping into a forward lunge — power from the legs, soft catch overhead. A true full-body athletic beat.

**Half-Kneeling Windmill:** drop to a half-kneeling stance (working-side knee down), bell overhead, and windmill from there — same eyes-on-bell hinge, now from the floor. This is where the flow lowers to the ground.
**Half-Kneeling Tactical Clean:** still half-kneeling — clean the bell smoothly to the rack from the floor position, controlling the whole path.
**Tactical Clean → Forward Stand:** clean as you rise — step the down leg forward and stand up out of the half-kneel in one motion, finishing racked. Brings you back to standing.
**Figure-8 Tactical Clean → Forward Stand:** a figure-8 pass into a tactical clean as you finish standing tall — the coordination beat that resets you upright.
**Skier Swing:** feet closer, swing the bell at your SIDE (not between the legs), driving it forward and up like a ski pole — quad-biased, hip-driven. Sets up the catch.

**Walter Catch:** off the skier swing, catch the bell softly at chest height and cradle it with BOTH hands — one on the handle, one cupping the ball up near the sternum — absorbing with soft arms and a braced core. Quiet, controlled catch; light bell. Closes the round before switching sides.

tips: This is ONE long flow — the fourteen moves connect seamlessly, no pausing between them. Grooving the sequence is the whole point.
Single LIGHT bell, 1–2 easy rounds per side. It's long and a little confusing on purpose; don't chase load or round count — chase remembering what comes next.

The half-kneeling sub-sequence (beats 9–12) is the tricky part: you lower to the floor (half-kneeling windmill → half-kneeling clean) and then stand back up (tactical clean forward stand → figure-8 clean forward stand). Walk it slowly the first few times.
Overhead-heavy in spots (windmills, press, snatch, catch) — pack the shoulder DOWN on every overhead beat, keep the load conservative, and back off if the right shoulder flares.
Run the whole 14-move chain on one side, then the other. Good as light Tuesday practice on a new flow.
